question: ABCD is a trapezium in which BC ∥ AD and AC = CD. If ∠ABC = 70° and ∠BAC = 62°, then what is the measure of ∠ACD (in degree)?
solution:
**Given:**

ABCD is a trapezium in which BC ∥ AD and AC = CD

∠ABC = 70°

∠BAC = 62°

**Formula Used:**

In triangle ABC: ∠ACB = 180° − (∠ABC + ∠BAC)

Angles on the same side of parallel lines are supplementary: ∠BAD + ∠ABC = 180°

∠CAD = ∠BAD − ∠BAC

In isosceles triangle ACD (AC = CD): ∠CAD = ∠ADC

Sum of angles in triangle ACD = 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e62a0e64edfd3a474e6b29f547ae889344d55dc1535b5019a85e40660fde0445.png] 

⇒ ∠ACB = 180° − (70° + 62°)

⇒ ∠ACB = 180° − 132°

⇒ ∠ACB = 48°

⇒ ∠BAD = 180° − 70°

⇒ ∠BAD = 110°

⇒ ∠CAD = 110° − 62°

⇒ ∠CAD = 48°

⇒ ∠ADC = 48° (since AC = CD)

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − (48° + 48°)

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − 96°

⇒ ∠ACD = 84°

**∴ The correct answer is 84°.**
